messages:
marty: Heads-up — we should decide how SLA-aware routing interacts with dedicated pool autoscaling. Current autoscaler only sees aggregate intent; it doesn't know per-tenant SLOs. We saw a 95th tail spike yesterday when several tenants with strict latency SLOs hit cold allocations.

lina: Agree. My proposal: annotate intents with an slo_class label (gold/silver/best-effort) and have the autoscaler maintain separate headroom targets per slo_class. That way gold gets reserved burst capacity.

alex: Curious about cost impact — separate headroom per class may raise idle GPU minutes. How do we bound it?

marty: Two levers: (1) soft headroom vs hard reservation — soft means we keep a credit pool that can be stolen by lower classes during sustained demand, (2) dynamic shrink based on recent miss-rate for the slo_class.

jordan: We should be explicit about admission behaviour. If a gold request can't be placed in its dedicated lane, we either: route to hosted fallback, queue with tight timeout, or preempt lower-class tasks. Which do we prefer?

lina: Prefer preempt lower-class tasks when possible. Hosted fallback is last resort for PII customers. Queueing risks violating client latency SLOs.

sam: Ops concern — preemption complexity + burst credit accounting will be a pain. Need strong telemetry: per-class preempt counts, preempt_latency, and cost delta. Also rollout plan: start with simulation based on logs before flipping live.

alex: For simulation, do we have traces with per-tenant SLO tags? We can replay by augmenting traces with synthetic slo_class based on tenant metadata.

jordan: Yes, we can map top-200 tenants to classes and run our admission & autoscale sim. I'll sketch a sim job.

marty: Implementation sketch (control-plane changes):
```yaml
intent: {
  tenant_id: string,
  tokens_est: int,
  slo_class: enum(gold,silver,best_effort),
  priority: int
}
```
Autoscaler will consume intents and produce per-class target_headroom and a global reserved_credits ledger. Controllers then enforce via placement decisions and preemption hooks.

lina: Question: where to store reserved_credits ledger? Operator DB or in-memory leader? If operator restarts we must persist credits to avoid double-counting.

sam: Persist in k8s CRD or central datastore (postgres). CRD means slow writes, but visible to kubectl. Postgres gives consistency and easier queries. I'd pick Postgres.

alex: On the placement side, runtime needs an admission API change: Accept intent.slo_class and return admission_result {route: dedicated|burst|hosted, preempt_candidates: [task_id]}. Keep it minimal so runtime change surface is small.

jordan: Can we make admission_result opaque and let controller interpret? That keeps operator control plane flexible.

marty: Tradeoffs: putting logic in controller (central) = simpler reasoning and global optima, but more blast radius on controller failures. Pushing to nodes (distributed) reduces central load but makes global fairness harder. I vote central for now, with circuit-breakers & read-only fallbacks.

lina: Agree central first. Also add a degradation policy: if controller unavailable, nodes fallback to best-effort admission with conservative limits.

sam: Testing plan:
- offline sim against 30d traffic with synthetic slo_class mapping
- small canary on a dedicated pool, enable preemption for low-volume tenants only
- metrics: 95th latency per class, preempt rate, effective GPU utilization, cost delta

alex: Add an A/B where half of gold traffic goes to a pool with conservative headroom and half to baseline to compare missed-slo counts.

marty: Rollout checklist:
- implement intent.slo_class + autoscaler per-class headroom (control-plane)
- implement reserved_credits ledger (postgres)
- admission API change (runtime + controller)
- sim + offline replay
- canary with monitoring dashboard + alert for gold_miss_rate > 0.5%

lina: One more operational detail: we need a knob for "eviction grace" per class so preempted tasks have a short drain window (200-500ms) to flush logs. Also record task state to speed up cold-start when requeued.

jordan: That implies we need faster checkpointing for KV cache or prefer keep-alive lease for warm workers. Potential refactor in runtime.

sam: Noted — add runtime ticket to expose checkpoint hooks.

marty: Open question for design decision doc: do we expose slo_class to tenants (self-service) or derive it from billing tiers? I lean billing-driven initially to avoid tenants gaming the system.

lina: Agreed billing-driven first. Later expose as opt-in with governance.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled job created -> infra/sim/adaptive-sla-replay (eta: next week) :white_check_mark:

marty: Action items:
- jordan: prototype replay sim and share numbers (due in 5d)
- alex: cost/ROI model for per-class headroom (due in 7d)
- lina: draft RFC with API details and rollout plan (due in 10d)
- sam: add postgres CRD vs Postgres write-up + migration checklist (due in 7d)

lina: Thanks — will start RFC draft. If anyone objects to central-first approach speak up now, otherwise I'll write it up.

alex: 👍 no objections from me.

jordan: 👍

sam: 👍

marty: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after sim results.
